overview: The meeting reviewed Design Option D 1.1 for the Medford High School project, focusing on the requirements for entirely new construction. Key discussions addressed MSBA mandates for a separate pool facility and the financial and logistical impacts of the proposed building footprint.

items.title: Option D and MSBA Pool Requirements
items.summary: Option D involves entirely new construction and requires the pool to be a standalone project with separate utilities, procurement, and a dedicated debt override vote. Matt Rice confirmed that the MSBA will not cost-share for the pool, making it a Medford-only expense.

items.title: Site Footprint and Modular Classroom Impacts
items.summary: The design requires a high volume of modular classrooms because the new footprint encroaches on existing wings to avoid building an eight-story structure. Maintaining a lower height is intended to improve student mobility and preserve ground-floor access for vocational and early education programs.

items.title: Cost Drivers for Option D 1.1
items.summary: This option is the most expensive due to high-rise building code requirements, the quantity of modular classrooms, and the inclusion of a synthetic turf field over parking.

subject: High School Design Option D 1.1 Review
